verses.1: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Gather the harvest year after year — feast and feast, for you have devoured, you have devoured, O Moab!
verses.2: For I will confound Ariel and her wealth and splendor will be mine.
verses.3: I will encircle you like David, and set a barricade around you, and raise towers over you.
verses.4: And your words will sink to the ground, and your speech will be buried in the dust; your voice will be like a whisper from the earth, and your words will barely rise above the ground.
verses.5: And her wealth will be like dust swept from a wall, and the host of her oppressors like a passing wind — and it will all vanish suddenly.
verses.6: From the LORD of Hosts it will come — judgment with thunder and earthquake, with a loud voice, a storm and a consuming fire.
verses.7: And it will be as if a dream in the night to the wealth of all the nations that have gathered against Jerusalem, to all the warriors and the besiegers, and to all who press hard against her.
verses.8: Like one who dreams of eating, and awakens hungry; or one who dreams of drinking, and awakens thirsty — so will the wealth of all the nations that have gathered on Mount Zion be.
verses.9: Be amazed, be stunned, be stunned and cry out! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
verses.10: For the LORD has poured out a spirit of drowsiness on you; He has closed your eyes, the eyes of the prophets, and the heads of the seers.
verses.11: And the vision will become to you like a sealed book — they give it to one who knows letters, saying, "Read this," and he says, "I cannot read, for it is sealed."
verses.12: And they give the book to one who does not know letters, saying, "Read this," and he says, "I do not know how to read."
verses.13: And the Lord said, "Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me, and their reverence for me is but a command learned by rote."
verses.14: Therefore I will proceed to perform wonders against this people, wonders and wonders; the wisdom of their wise ones will vanish, and the understanding of their understanding ones will be hidden.
verses.15: Woe to those who plot in secret, whose deeds are done in darkness, and who say, "Who sees us? Who knows what we do?"
verses.16: Are you not as clay to the potter, who says of the work he has made, "This is only a thing of my hands," and the vessel says to the one who shaped it, "You did not understand"?
verses.17: Is it not soon that Lebanon will be turned into a forest and Carmel into a grove?
verses.18: In that day the deaf will hear the words of a book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of darkness and out of gloom.
verses.19: The meek among Jacob will take joy, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
verses.20: For the violent will disappear, and the arrogant will come to an end, and all who act in iniquity will be cut off.
verses.21: Those who cause a man to stumble with words — and those who set a trap at the gate, who turn the righteous aside with empty arguments —
verses.22: therefore thus says the LORD concerning the house of Jacob, whom He redeemed from Abraham: Jacob will not be put to shame, nor will his face be blushed.
verses.23: For when my children see the work of my hands among them, they will sanctify my name, and they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will revere the God of Israel.
verses.24: And those who err in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will learn to listen.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "Ariel" is a poetic name for Jerusalem, though some interpretations suggest it may refer to a specific location or symbol.
- v. 16: The metaphor of the potter and clay is used to emphasize God's sovereignty and human dependence.
- v. 17: "Lebanon" and "Carmel" are used symbolically to illustrate transformation and renewal.
- v. 21: The reference to "setting a trap at the gate" alludes to unjust behavior in public settings, likely legal or civic.
raw:
[1] Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Gather the harvest year after year — feast and feast, for you have devoured, you have devoured, O Moab!

[2] For I will confound Ariel and her wealth and splendor will be mine.

[3] I will encircle you like David, and set a barricade around you, and raise towers over you.

[4] And your words will sink to the ground, and your speech will be buried in the dust; your voice will be like a whisper from the earth, and your words will barely rise above the ground.

[5] And her wealth will be like dust swept from a wall, and the host of her oppressors like a passing wind — and it will all vanish suddenly.

[6] From the LORD of Hosts it will come — judgment with thunder and earthquake, with a loud voice, a storm and a consuming fire.

[7] And it will be as if a dream in the night to the wealth of all the nations that have gathered against Jerusalem, to all the warriors and the besiegers, and to all who press hard against her.

[8] Like one who dreams of eating, and awakens hungry; or one who dreams of drinking, and awakens thirsty — so will the wealth of all the nations that have gathered on Mount Zion be.

[9] Be amazed, be stunned, be stunned and cry out! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.

[10] For the LORD has poured out a spirit of drowsiness on you; He has closed your eyes, the eyes of the prophets, and the heads of the seers.

[11] And the vision will become to you like a sealed book — they give it to one who knows letters, saying, "Read this," and he says, "I cannot read, for it is sealed."

[12] And they give the book to one who does not know letters, saying, "Read this," and he says, "I do not know how to read."

[13] And the Lord said, "Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me, and their reverence for me is but a command learned by rote."

[14] Therefore I will proceed to perform wonders against this people, wonders and wonders; the wisdom of their wise ones will vanish, and the understanding of their understanding ones will be hidden.

[15] Woe to those who plot in secret, whose deeds are done in darkness, and who say, "Who sees us? Who knows what we do?"

[16] Are you not as clay to the potter, who says of the work he has made, "This is only a thing of my hands," and the vessel says to the one who shaped it, "You did not understand"?

[17] Is it not soon that Lebanon will be turned into a forest and Carmel into a grove?

[18] In that day the deaf will hear the words of a book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of darkness and out of gloom.

[19] The meek among Jacob will take joy, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

[20] For the violent will disappear, and the arrogant will come to an end, and all who act in iniquity will be cut off.

[21] Those who cause a man to stumble with words — and those who set a trap at the gate, who turn the righteous aside with empty arguments —

[22] therefore thus says the LORD concerning the house of Jacob, whom He redeemed from Abraham: Jacob will not be put to shame, nor will his face be blushed.

[23] For when my children see the work of my hands among them, they will sanctify my name, and they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will revere the God of Israel.

[24] And those who err in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will learn to listen.

---
Notes
- v. 1: "Ariel" is a poetic name for Jerusalem, though some interpretations suggest it may refer to a specific location or symbol.
- v. 16: The metaphor of the potter and clay is used to emphasize God's sovereignty and human dependence.
- v. 17: "Lebanon" and "Carmel" are used symbolically to illustrate transformation and renewal.
- v. 21: The reference to "setting a trap at the gate" alludes to unjust behavior in public settings, likely legal or civic.
